indexEntry.body:
General Admission Requirements

The minimum admission requirements are expressed in terms of the current Ontario secondary school curriculum. Presentation of the minimum requirements guarantees only that the applicant will be considered for admission. In many programs, the number of qualified applicants may exceed the number of spaces available. In this event, the admission process will be based on a competition for the spaces available, and the majority of the students admitted usually have averages substantially above the minimum requirements.

Applicants educated outside of the Ontario secondary school system must meet admission average requirements and present course work equivalent to required Ontario Grade 12 U (university level) and/or M (university/college level) courses in addition to an equivalent level of education. These applicants are required to submit official transcripts for all years spent in secondary and post-secondary education. Transcripts must indicate subjects studied, the grades received, and an interpretation of the grading systems used.

Applicants who are refused admission to a particular program may be considered for admission to other programs for which they satisfy the specific subject and average requirements if spaces are available.

English Language Requirements

The official language of instruction at the University of Waterloo is English. It is the responsibility of the University to ensure that its undergraduate students have sufficient English language skills to cope with the demands of the academic curriculum, as well as, for many, the communication skills to be successful in co-operative education programs.

The English language requirements are distinct from and in addition to Ontario Grade 12 U (university level) English (or equivalent) where it is stated as an admission requirement.
The University reserves the right to request an English proficiency test score and/or to withdraw any offer of admission if the applicant fails to meet the minimum English language requirements for the program to which they have applied.

Find out more about the English language requirements including proof of proficiency and acceptable test results.

Tuberculosis Skin Test

Newly admitted students who have been living and/or pursuing their education outside Canada must have documented evidence that they have had a recent tuberculosis (TB) skin test before undertaking studies at the University. Upon arrival or while attending the University, students must be prepared to present documentation if requested by a University official. This documentation must include the type of skin test taken, the date performed, and the number of millimetres of induration. Students who are requested to provide documentation but are unable to do so, or students who are unsure about the safety of the needles and/or injection procedures in their previous country of residence, must report to Health Services upon arrival on campus. Where applicable, Health Services will administer the TB skin test. There is a cost for this service.

In addition, students who have travelled outside Canada or the United States for four weeks or longer should contact their health care provider to discuss the need for TB skin testing.

Admission Requirements by Application Group

Applicants From Ontario Secondary Schools

Students who will be completing the Ontario secondary school (OSS) curriculum must present the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD), including a minimum of six Grade 12 U (university level) and/or M (university/college level) courses. These courses must include all required courses, as specified for each program. Required courses must be at the Grade 12 U level unless otherwise specified.

An overall average of 80% on the best six Grade 12 U and/or M courses, including the required courses, is normally the minimum requirement for admission consideration. Higher averages are required for admission to programs for which the number of qualified applicants exceeds the number of places available. The actual minimum averages required for these programs are determined each year on the basis of the number of applicants, their qualifications, and the number of available spaces.

In some programs, applicants may be considered for early conditional admission based on their Grade 11 academic record, their Grade 12 record to date, and other factors.

Find out more about program-specific admission requirements.

Applicants From Other Canadian Provinces and Territories

Applicants from other provinces and territories must present a secondary school graduation (Grade 12) diploma. Applicants from Quebec who complete the Secondary V Diploma must present at least one year of the Quebec Collèges d'enseignement général et professionnel (CEGEP) program to be considered for admission.

Find out more about program-specific requirements by province.

Applicants From Other Education Systems or Countries

All programs at the University have prerequisites or subjects that are required for admission. Applicants from educational systems outside Ontario must present the equivalents of these prerequisites at the highest secondary school level possible to be considered for admission.

All international credentials presented by an applicant are subject to review by the admissions committee for the faculty to which they have applied. In some cases, details on curriculum content and depth of study may be requested by the admissions committee to review equivalence to the Ontario system and additional Advanced Placement (AP) or university-level credits may be required.

Find out more about program-specific requirements for common systems of study and national curricula outside of Canada.

Home-Schooled Students

Home-schooled students will be considered individually by the admissions committee(s) for the program(s) to which they have applied. Evidence must be provided that the student has completed an academic level equivalent to the minimum standard required for the program(s) to which they have applied.

Find out more about recommendations for home-schooled students to provide proof of academic proficiency. Home-schooled students are encouraged to contact admissions directly to obtain program-specific recommendations.

Mature Students

For admission purposes, the University’s definition of a mature student varies by faculty. In all cases, it is not defined by age but by level of academic background and number of years since the applicant last attended formal secondary school. All faculties require a minimum number of specific Ontario Grade 12 U (university level) and/or M (university/college level) courses (or equivalents) in addition to meeting their definition of a mature student.

Applicants who have previously attended university or college are not considered as mature students for admission purposes. They should follow the admission requirements for applicants from college or university.

Find out more about faculty-specific mature student policies and program-specific requirements.

  • See Faculty of Mathematics information in this Calendar.

Transfer Students

Applicants with post-secondary education experience should review the transferring to Waterloo information.
